headline: ULA Vulcan Centaur fails during launch with 40 Amazon satellites aboard
summary: A Vulcan Centaur rocket failed during launch on the fifteenth of November with 40 Amazon satellites aboard, and no cause has been published.
Amazon's next launch is on Europe's Ariane 6, flight VA271, with 36 Amazon Leo satellites no earlier than the twenty-third of November.
Australia has signed the Horizon Europe agreement, which opens space and research funding.
Japan's Synspective has released first imagery from its twelfth satellite.
The Rome meeting of the fifteenth of December and the Artemis proposals due on the eighth of December remain the next fixed dates.
bottom_line: The Vulcan failure leaves Ariane 6 flight VA271 as the next Amazon Leo launch in view, with no cause or return date published for Vulcan. The next date that matters is the twenty-third of November, the earliest date for VA271.
audio_script: Good morning. It is Tuesday, the seventeenth of November, and this is the Sovereign Space ATLAS briefing. A United States Vulcan Centaur rocket has failed during launch with 40 Amazon satellites aboard. Australia has signed the European Union's Horizon Europe agreement. And Japan's Synspective has released first imagery from its twelfth satellite. A Vulcan Centaur rocket carrying 40 Amazon satellites failed during launch on the fifteenth of November. No cause has been published, and no date has been given for the next Vulcan flight. The loss falls on Amazon's constellation, which is also due to fly on Europe's Ariane 6. That flight, VA271, carries 36 Amazon Leo satellites and is set for the twenty-third of November at the earliest. Whether it holds that date is now the date to watch. Separately, SpaceX caught a Starship upper stage after about twenty-two hours in orbit, a first for the program. In Europe, the vote of the tenth of November has no published outcome. The Rome meeting stands for the fifteenth of December. ArianeGroup completed a hot-fire test of its Prometheus reusable engine on the sixth of November, on the test bench of the German aerospace centre DLR. Ariane 6 flight VA271 is the next European launch, no earlier than the twenty-third of November. In Ukraine, President Zelenskyy said on the twelfth of November that Starlink speed restrictions had been recorded for several days. SpaceX has made no statement. The hope of Starshield service for Ukraine by mid-2027 is unchanged. No new date has been set. In Sweden, the national space agency has noted that Voyager 1 is reaching a distance of one light-day from Earth. The agency's next Space Day is on the eighteenth of February, 2027. In Spain, PLD Space plans to double its workforce in Teruel by 2029 to consolidate its test capacity for European launchers. The regional government of Valencia has also granted almost two million euros to Iceye Spain to build satellites in Paterna. In Central Asia, a joint satellite of the Turkic states is to be sent to orbit in 2027. No launch date or provider has been published, so the next date is still to be set. In Türkiye, a new microsatellite is due to launch in 2028. In Algeria, the space agency ASAL has marked ten years of Alsat-2B in orbit. It has also given an account of its attendance at the international committee on satellite navigation systems, held in Goa, India, from the twenty-fifth to the thirtieth of October. In Japan, Synspective has announced first imagery from its twelfth satellite. The Mars moons probe MMX remains on its transfer orbit, and no arrival date has been given. In Australia, the government has signed the Horizon Europe agreement, which opens European space and research funding to Australian teams. Gilmour Space's Eris TestFlight1 was named Engineers Australia Project of the Year on the thirteenth of November. In Mexico, 540 million pesos were committed in March to launch four satellites for security and climate monitoring. No launch date has been given. In Venezuela, the space agency ABAE has presented in Vienna its progress in satellite monitoring of river basins. What we are tracking this week is the cause of the Vulcan failure, and whether Ariane 6 flight VA271 leaves on the twenty-third of November at the earliest. What we are tracking this month is the NASA Artemis proposals, due on the eighth of December, and the Rome meeting on the fifteenth of December. NASA made moon base contract awards on the ninth of November. The Blue Origin return in January 2027 is still unconfirmed, and the thirtieth of October deadline at the American aviation regulator passed with no decision on file. The heads-up dates are the twenty-third of November, the eighth of December, the fifteenth of December, and the eighteenth of February. That is the briefing for Tuesday, the seventeenth of November. Thank you for listening to the Sovereign Space ATLAS briefing. The next edition follows tomorrow morning, and it will carry any word on the Vulcan cause or on the Ariane 6 flight date.

global.title: ULA Vulcan Centaur fails during launch with 40 Amazon satellites
global.summary: A Vulcan Centaur rocket failed during launch on the fifteenth of November with 40 Amazon satellites aboard. No cause or next-flight date is published.
global.why: Amazon's constellation now leans on other launchers, including Ariane 6 flight VA271. The failure is a setback for the United States heavy-lift market outside SpaceX.
global.bar: Cause and return-to-flight date not in sources; do not characterise.

global.title: Voyager 1 reaches a distance of one light-day from Earth
global.summary: Voyager 1 is reaching one light-day from Earth, as noted by the Swedish National Space Agency and in Spanish press on the fifteenth of November.
global.why: It is a distance milestone for the longest-running deep-space mission. No decision or program change follows from it.
global.bar: Context item; exact crossing date not given in sources.

global.title: NASA awards moon base development contracts
global.summary: NASA made major moon base contract awards on the ninth of November. Artemis dates are unchanged, with proposals due on the eighth of December.
global.why: The awards set the industrial base for the lunar program. The proposal deadline is the next fixed date.
global.bar: Standing thread, not new; no NASA page in packet.

items.title: Zelenskyy says Starlink speed restrictions recorded in Ukraine for several days
items.summary: President Zelenskyy said on the twelfth of November that restrictions were recorded for several days. SpaceX has not commented, and the mid-2027 Starshield hope is unchanged.
items.why: Ukraine's communications depend on a commercial service it does not control. No date has been set for any change.
items.bar: Standing; Zelenskyy quote carried from earlier filing, no fresh source.
